correctness.rationale: With u=gamma_R/b>0 and v=gamma_T/b>0, the source stationary 1F2 characteristic function has even moments (1/2)_m(v/2)_m/[((u+v)/2)_m((u+1)/2)_m]. For resonance v=u+1+2n, put c=(u+1)/2 and B_{u,n}=Gamma(u+n+1/2)/(sqrt(pi) Gamma(u+n)) (1-x²)^{u+n-1}; the differential operator Hf=-(xf)'/2 sends moment m to m times itself (boundary terms vanish before every differentiation). Thus (c)_n^{-1}prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(H+c+j)B_{u,n} has every hypergeometric stationary even moment, is even, compactly supported, and equals the unique stationary distribution by compact moment determinacy. It becomes (1-x²)^{u-1} times a polynomial in x² and hence analytic at 0. Conversely the explicit inverse Fourier branch has coefficient proportional to 1/Gamma((u+1-v)/2) times |x|^{v-1}. Except on resonance, nonodd v yields a nonanalytic fractional branch; odd positive v creates a log |x| term via the nonzero pole residue, so remains nonanalytic off resonance. The n=0 beta density and u=1,n=1 analytic density 3(1+x²)/8 normalize correctly; direct moment m=1,2 gives 2/5,9/35 as the general formula. This is conditional on the primary source's exact transform, which was actually read. No inference from finite checks is needed for the all-parameter statement.
